# Apple framework reference

`pencilkit-reference.json` is unmodified numerical output from BoardEject's
[macOS validation run 34703744158](https://github.com/royalpinto007/boardeject/actions/runs/34703744158).
The public `tools/native-validation/main.swift` generates a four-control pen
stroke, serializes and reloads it using PencilKit, then samples its path at
parametric intervals of 0.125 and applies its translation.

This is Apple-generated reference data, not a Freeform clipboard capture.
It validates this centerline case and endpoint behavior only. It does not
validate masked strokes, variable-width rendering, or native group transforms.
The fixture contains no user board data.

## Width and geometric-mask references

`variable-width.drawing`, `masked-gap.drawing`, and `masked-gap-reference.json`
come from [run 34765945034](https://github.com/royalpinto007/boardeject/actions/runs/34765945034),
generated by `tools/native-validation/main.swift` at commit `3ae6d61`.
They contain only seven scripted control points and a constructed two-rectangle
mask, serialized and reloaded by Apple PencilKit. No user board or machine paths
are included. The original artifacts are preserved separately.

Apple reports visible parametric ranges `[0, 2.25]` and `[3.75, 6]` for the
masked case. The current decoder retains a top-level stroke field 11 in rawData
but exposes no visibleRanges. BoardEject therefore omits this masked stroke;
rendering the full centerline would restore the hidden gap.

The unmasked fixture verifies decoding widths 2 through 14 and force 0.125
through 0.875. Output still uses an explicitly reported uniform-width
approximation. These are **Apple framework decoder references**, not Freeform
captures, physical pressure input, or proof of Freeform eraser behavior.
